evidence: You can walk or ride the track in either direction, but it's best to start from Meretoto/Ship Cove.
The final hour’s walking is on an easy path through mature beech forest to Anakiwa.
At Anakiwa are a carpark, shelter, toilets and phone near the track end, and a public jetty opposite the Outward Bound school.

doubts: The track is one way from Meretoto/Ship Cove to Anakiwa. The page says it can be walked or ridden in either direction, but that is not a separate way, so the reverse is not recorded. Torea Saddle is taken as the road-end feature F1 (where Queen Charlotte Track meets Torea Road) and Anakiwa as F3 (where Queen Charlotte Track meets Anakiwa Road); the text does not name the features. The Camp Bay bypass by a direct track to Kenepuru Saddle and the mountain bike alternative along Kenepuru Road are not recorded as ways: the first is a bypass with no description of its own, and the second is a bike option. The Cowshed Bay campsite is described in the Camp Bay to Torea Saddle section, but its position on the track is not stated, so it is listed after Torea Saddle. The Te Mahia Saddle is named in the text but is not a map entry. Mistletoe Saddle (access by road) is not in the names list, and Mistletoe Bay in the walk is a different place. Campsites are listed as vias, not huts; the private cabins, hostels and motels are not named DOC huts, so the huts list is empty. The Peninsula Walk is recorded from null because the text does not say where it leaves the track. DOC's '3-5 days' and '73.5 km one way' are copied; the section distances in the text add to about 71 km.
